text.p: Investment bank Renaissance Capital said on Tuesday it had maintained its buy recommendations on LUKoil ordinary and preferred shares.
On Monday OAO Neftyanaya Kompaniya LUKoil announced a rise in oil output and a small rise in pre-tax profit in 1996.
"We maintain our positive long-term view of the company and recommend purchase of both the ordinary and preferred shares," it said in its daily monitor of the Russian markets.
Renaissance noted LUKoil had performed exceptionally strongly in the new year rally of leading Russian shares.

"However, with the possibility that profitability has stagnated for the time being, higher relative valuations and a possible $1 billion share offering looming at year-end, we anticipate that LUKoil will track the market for most of 1997," it said.

But the stock has significant long-term upside potential, as the first of its many growth projects in Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan will begin production in late 1997 and it is continuing to make improvements at its refineries, it said.
Renaissance said profitability appeared to have declined despite the improvement in operational performance.
LUKoil said pre-tax profits, according to preliminary unaudited figures to Russian accounting standards, had risen to 3.7 trillion roubles in 1996 from 3.425 trillion in 1995.

LUKoil's full-year profit estimate compares with a pre-tax profit for the first nine months of 3.14 trillion, suggesting the fourth quarter was significantly less profitable than the preceding quarters, Renaissance said.
"If these figures are confirmed over the coming months, the actual decline in pre-tax profitability will be viewed negatively by the market," it said.
